extracted.intended_audience: Black speculative fiction writers (African diaspora and African continent) submitting prose, poetry, or art to FIYAH
extracted.subtask_description: Submission guidelines for FIYAH, a quarterly speculative fiction magazine prioritizing Black authors; covers eligibility, content restrictions, formatting, length, rights/payment, art guidelines, theme preferences, and response procedures for prose, poetry, and art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility (Black authorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH is a quarterly speculative fiction magazine that features stories by and about Black people of the African Diaspora. This definition is globally inclusive (Black anywhere in the world) and also applies to mixed/biracial and Afro-appended people regardless of gender identity or orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We are only accepting submission from authors from the African diaspora and the African continent because #BlackWritersMatter. This is an intersectional definition of Blackness, and we strongly encourage submissions from women, members of the LGBTQIA community, and members from other underrepresented communities within the African diaspora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished work only / no reprints or fan fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: We only consider unpublished work, and we do not consider reprints (work that has been published in another magazine or on your blog or other social media) or fan fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your submission must not have been published elsewhere in any form prior to submission to FIYAH.

rubrics_metrics.name: No multiple or simultaneous submissions (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept multiple submissions for fiction, so please wait until you have heard a response before submitting again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting under different aliases does not evade this policy; we will recognize your writing style. The page also states 'We do not accept simultaneous submissions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No resubmissions of previously rejected work
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not resubmit previously rejected stories or poems in a new submission period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions are by editorial solicitation only; previously rejected pieces sent again without solicitation will be rejected automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIYAH no-AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH is committed to publishing only those works which are entirely created by and original to the human author attached to each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted under false pretenses, the piece in violation of our no-AI policy will be rejected and the author will be banned from future submissions to FIYAH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content rejection triggers (graphic/harms)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will immediately reject work that feature any of the following without providing feedback: Graphic depictions of rape or sexual assault; Needless brutalization of women and children; Depictions of brutalization or abuse of people with disabilities; Graphic abuse of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, we reserve the right to reject and not provide feedback on work we believe may be harmful to our readers. Work that has elements of homophobia, fatphobia, colorism, ageism etc. that go unchallenged will not find a home with us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and fiction categories
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions of short fiction 2,000 – 7,000 words and novelettes up to 15,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note from editor: 'Novelettes are a tough sale. I’d prefer to acquire two 7k word stories than one at 14k.' This affects acquisition likelihood for longer pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry length and submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry submissions should be no more than 1,000 words. For poetry, you may submit up to four (4) separate poems, one (1) poem per form submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each poem with its own form entry; do not place multiple poems in a single form submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose and poetry formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be submitted in proper short story manuscript format with your name, email address, and the story’s total word count on the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For our purposes, you do not need to include a mailing address or phone number. All submissions should be in .doc/.docx format. The page links to an example of proper short story manuscript format and a post on writing a professional cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: General editorial taste for prose (quality & themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are looking for brave works of speculative short fiction by authors from the African continent and diaspora that reject regressive ideas of blackness, respectability politics, and stereotype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We want your bravest, blackest, most difficult to sell stories. We want stories that are well written, of high quality, and generally easy to read on a screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry editorial taste
rubrics_metrics.description: What we want in speculative poetry is verse that struggles, reveals, instructs, comforts, and fights back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We are looking for weird, complex, honest and challenging work with a clear speculative element from Black authors. See the Poetry Editor's post for more specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue/theme-specific preferences (e.g., Conjuring Academies)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 40th issue (Conjuring Academies & Spellbound Scholars) they are enthusiastically accepting submissions featuring magical schools and related tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific encouragements: Pan-African university for gifted mages; non-Western settings for instruction; stories that examine and challenge hierarchical relationships in school; whimsy, joy, and humor; stunning worldbuilding with well-developed characters; genre-bending is welcome if idea supports it. Editor note: 'Particularly interested in whimsy, joy, and humor. Stunning worldbuilding always makes me lean in—flat characters will make me reluctantly pass.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submission fit and portfolio expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists should submit portfolios or work samples which illustrate an understanding of composition, and which feature fantastical elements and/or can be categorized as fantasy, science-fiction, horror, and their related subgenres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard portraiture and/or still life will not be a good fit. In keeping with our mission, we prioritize Black creators as the face and content of our magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rates for prose/poetry/nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment schedule for 2023 (USD): Short stories (2,000 – 7,000 words): $0.08/word; Novelettes (<15,000 words): $0.08/word; Poetry: $50 USD; Nonfiction: $0.10/word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIYAH is a SFWA-qualifying market. Works of prose published with us count toward SFWA membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights FIYAH acquires for prose
rubrics_metrics.description: FIYAH will claim first world electronic rights, nonexclusive archival rights, and nonexclusive anthology rights to your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They buy rights to publish your story on FIYAH’s website and in electronic issues of the magazine. Your story cannot appear anywhere else online or in print prior to submission, or for 180 days after FIYAH publishes it. After that it can be reprinted online, in a magazine, or in an anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art payment and rights terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissions pay $400.00 USD for original artwork and FIYAH purchases rights to First Use and six months exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should be aware FIYAH purchases first use rights plus six months exclusivity; consult the art submission link for portfolio submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous FIYAH authors resubmission wait period
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers previously published in an issue of FIYAH must wait 1 year or 4 issues to submit work again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works submitted before that time is up will be automatically rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and querying policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Response time will vary by volume of submissions. You may query after 45 days using email submissions[at]fiyahlitmag.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When querying include the date you submitted and the title of your story. The site also suggests tracking submissions with Duotrope and The Submission Grinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system / accessibility and confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are collected via a simple form; you will see a confirmation message when the form is completed, indicating your submission was successfully received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They acknowledge the form may not be accessible to disabled users; if you require an alternative means of submission, contact team[@]fiyahlitmag.com and they will arrange one. Note: You will not receive an e-mailed confirmation.
